attachments.origin_landmark: inferior edge of internal oblique and the inguinal ligament
attachments.insertion_landmark: pubic tubercle, via loops over the spermatic cord

innervation.root_levels: L1-L2 (genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve)

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: A derivative of internal oblique carried down with the descending testis. The cremasteric reflex it mediates -- stroking the medial thigh (L1 sensory, ilioinguinal) elevates the testis -- is lost in testicular torsion, and is one of the few reflexes with sensory and motor limbs in different nerves.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Not ultrasound-guided in the only published human report: electromyography-guided percutaneous injection into each cremaster muscle at the level of the superficial inguinal ring/proximal scrotum, along the course of the spermatic cord.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Superficial to the spermatic cord proper, within the cremasteric fascia/muscle loops that surround it.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: EMG confirmation of needle placement within contracting cremaster fibers, given the muscle's thin, discontinuous loop-like arrangement around the cord.
structures_at_risk: spermatic cord contents (vas deferens, testicular vessels), immediately deep to the muscle loops
ilioinguinal nerve, running with the cord and providing the sensory limb of the cremasteric reflex
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: A single published human case: EMG-guided botulinum toxin A (15 MU right, 10 MU left) relieved postoperative bilateral cremaster muscle synkinesis (aberrant reinnervation after oesophagectomy) for an average of 8 weeks. A genuine but isolated clinical lead -- a single case report of a rare indication (synkinesis, not spasticity or pain) -- rather than an established technique; a separate experimental rat study showed the toxin paralyses cremaster on compound muscle action potential testing, supporting biological plausibility but not itself a human technique.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Ritter MA, Frese A, Dziewas R, Knecht S, Evers S (2006) Mov Disord 21(10):1787-1788, doi:10.1002/mds.21040 -- video case report of EMG-guided botulinum toxin A injection for cremaster muscle synkinesis (PubMed)
